column1: # BLOCK FAMILIES -- the `!!!` and `???` callouts, and which theme token paints
# each one.
# Written in a page as:
#     !!! warning "Rigging plot"        an open box
#     ??? note "Long detail"           a collapsed box
#     ???+ tip "Start open"            collapsible, open by default
# ⚠️ THE BODY MUST BE INDENTED FOUR SPACES. Python-Markdown's admonition
# processor calls `detab()` on the block after the `!!!` line: anything not
# indented becomes `theRest` and is re-inserted as a SEPARATE block. So an
# unindented body renders as a title-only box followed by a loose paragraph --
# which looks like a styling bug and is an authoring one.
# ⭐ THIS FILE ANSWERS Q14, WHICH WAS OPEN FROM 2026-08-04 TO 08-05. Before it,
# DL J20 recorded the state plainly: the block vocabulary was "defined NOWHERE
# -- two lines in mkdocs.yml turn the syntax on and that is all." So a reader
# could type twelve different callout colours and not one of them came from the
# design system. This is the largest surface on a documentation site and it was
# the last big one Material owned outright.
# ADDING OR RECOLOURING ONE IS A ROW HERE. No code change, no CSS change --
# docrender/blocks.py emits the rules as generated CSS, exactly like
# markers.py emits the marker class colours.
# TWO KINDS OF ROW: INHERITED AND DECLARED
# The first twelve are MATERIAL'S names. They are not names we chose and they
# are not ours to rename: `note`, `warning`, `danger` and the rest are what a
# reader TYPES, and Material ships an icon and a flavour rule keyed to each one.
# ⚠️ THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE LIST BEING CLOSED, and the original header
# implied it was. Python-Markdown's admonition extension matches `!!! ([\w\-]+)`
# and lowercases the word straight into a class, with NO validation -- verified
# in its source, not assumed. So any word has always rendered. `good` is the
# first family we DECLARE rather than inherit, and it sits below the twelve
# under its own heading so the boundary is legible here rather than in a commit.
# ⚠️ A DECLARED FAMILY NEEDS AN `icon`, AND THE FAILURE IS SUBTLE IF IT DOES
# NOT GET ONE. Material's base rule is unconditional:
#     .md-typeset .admonition-title::before {
#       background-color: $clr-blue-a200;
#       mask-image: var(--md-admonition-icon--note);      <- THE PENCIL
# Per-family rules override it. A family Material has never heard of therefore
# does not LOSE its icon -- it wears the note pencil, which reads as a styling
# near-miss rather than as an unfinished family.
# COLUMNS
# block   the word a reader types after `!!!` or `???`
# color   the token that paints it: any token this engine emits, or a hex
# icon    ONE OF MATERIAL'S TWELVE NAMES, borrowing that family's glyph.
#         BLANK on every inherited row, because Material already keys their
#         icons off the class name and a value there would be a second
#         statement of a fact Material owns.
# note    what the family MEANS, and why this token
# ⭐ `icon` NAMES A VARIABLE AND NEVER HOLDS IMAGE DATA, which is the whole
# reason this column is allowed to exist. An earlier version of this header
# refused an icon column outright, on the grounds that "changing one means
# authoring an SVG data URL, and image data does not belong in a colour table."
# That refusal stands. `--md-admonition-icon--success` is already defined by
# Material, so `icon: success` is a POINTER at something that exists.
# ⚠️ AND IT IS VALIDATED, because a wrong name is loud rather than quiet:
# `mask-image: var(--md-admonition-icon--nonsense)` is an undefined var with no
# fallback -> invalid at computed-value time -> `mask-image: none` -> no mask ->
# the ::before paints its full background-color as a solid 20x20px SQUARE.
# blocks.py refuses a name outside the twelve and reports it.
# 🔴 `data-1..4` WERE TRIED HERE FIRST AND THE MEASUREMENT REJECTED THEM. The
# first version of this file painted abstract / question / bug / example from the
# four chart-series tokens, on the argument that a chart series and a callout
# family want the same property: several colours that are mutually
# distinguishable and carry no meaning of their own.
# The reasoning held. The VALUES did not. Border contrast against the callout
# ground, measured in both schemes:
#     abstract  data-1   dark 4.45   LIGHT 2.08
#     question  data-2   dark 4.60   LIGHT 2.02
#     bug       data-3   dark 5.75   LIGHT 1.61
#     example   data-4   dark 5.97   LIGHT 1.55
# All four clear the 3.0 UI-edge floor in dark, all four fail it badly in light.
# ⚠️ AND THE CAUSE IS UPSTREAM, NOT HERE: `data-1..4` ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL IN ALL
# 39 ROWS of maw-themes vectors/colors.tsv. Same four hexes on every dark row and
# every light row of every theme. They are not theme-aware and never have been --
# authored once against a dark ground, then carried through the alt-band
# transposition faithfully, because that is what a transposition does.
# So they cannot be used as theme tokens by ANY consumer until real values exist,
# and that is a bigger finding than the four rows it cost. Raised upstream.
# ⚠️ SEMANTIC TOKENS ARE DELIBERATELY REUSED ACROSS FAMILIES. `failure`,
# `danger` and `bug` are all `bad`; `tip`, `success` and `good` are all `good`.
# Words that mean the same thing to a reader should not be different colours,
# and the icon already tells them apart.
# ⚠️ THREE ON ONE TOKEN IS ONE MORE THAN THAT ARGUMENT COMFORTABLY CARRIES,
# though. `tip` is advice, `success` is a thing that worked, and `good` is a
# positive POINTER -- which is a real third register in a venue context ("look
# here for first aid") and is also the point at which somebody should check the
# distinction still holds. If it cannot be stated on sight, cull one rather than
# letting three drift.
# 🚩 AND THE AUTHORING PAGE DISAGREES WITH THIS FILE. template-docs
# `authoring/writing.md` has a section headed "Only three, and each means
# something specific" -- note, warning, danger -- arguing a fourth type is
# exactly what the limit exists to prevent. PR #88 shipped twelve governed
# families and never touched it, so the document authors consult has been wrong
# since 2026-08-05 18:15. How many families are SANCTIONED is a policy question
# and belongs to Michael; this file only records what is PAINTED.
block
note
column4: the house voice. A note from us, so it takes the site's own identity colour rather than a semantic one.

column1: abstract
column4: A summary or TL;DR, in the secondary identity voice. Was data-1; see the warning above.

column1: info
column4: FINALLY A CONSUMER FOR `info`. The token has been emitted by every canonical theme and read by nothing since the join landed, because until now this engine had no surface that meant "informational".

column1: tip
column4: Advice that helps. Same meaning as success to a reader, same token.

column1: success
column4: Something worked or is confirmed. Shares `good` with tip on purpose.

column1: question
column4: An open question or FAQ. Shares `info`: a question and an informational aside are the same register, and the icon already tells them apart. Was data-2.

column1: warning
column4: Proceed carefully. The same token that paints every confidence marker chip, which is correct: both mean "do not lean on this yet".

column1: failure
column4: Something did not work. Shares `bad` with danger and bug.

column1: danger
column4: A hazard. In a venue and production context this is the one that matters most, and it must read as the same alarm as failure.

column1: bug
column4: A known defect. I argued for a separate colour -- a bug is a RECORD of something broken rather than a warning about it -- and dropped it: that distinction is not worth a border nobody can see in light mode. Was data-3.

column1: example
column4: A worked example. Quiet, like quote, and the FIRST CONSUMER of text-faint anywhere in this engine. Was data-4.

column1: quote
column4: A quotation. Deliberately the muted text colour and not a hue: a quote is quieter than the page, not a category of alert.

column1: # --- DECLARED BY US. Material has never heard of these, so each one MUST name
# --- an `icon` or it silently inherits the note pencil.
good
column4: A POSITIVE POINTER -- "look here for first aid", "this is the good entrance". Michael, 2026-08-05: "not a red box, but green positive render notes." Borrows the `success` check glyph, because Material defines that variable and this family has no glyph of its own. Measured on the callout ground: edge 5.00 dark / 4.45 light against a 3.0 floor, title-on-wash 8.41 / 10.55 against 4.5.
